title: The app sometimes forgets (disable) certain features that users have enabled (for example, lightswitch)

status.label: Needs targeted evidence

judgment.rationale: The original diagnostic archive and reproducible periodic reset are useful evidence, and a newer report says multiple modules can change state together, but the current discussion still does not identify the trigger or persistence boundary.
evidence: The original report includes a PowerToys bug report ZIP and says the reset recurs every few days.
The latest commenter reports the same class of unexpected enablement for Awake and Command Palette, suggesting the scope may extend beyond LightSwitch.
No current comment identifies whether the change occurs after restart, update, crash recovery, or settings-file replacement.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the trigger boundary and a fresh /bugreport captured immediately after the next occurrence before proposing a fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: A repository fix is not yet actionable because the selected lightweight pass did not find enough public evidence to identify the failing PowerToys code path.

issue_context.summary: Several PowerToys modules reportedly change enabled state without user action: the original report described LightSwitch disabling every few days, and a newer report describes previously disabled Awake and Command Palette becoming enabled. Existing diagnostics did not show a crash, but the trigger and settings persistence path remain unresolved.
known_information: Original report: PowerToys 0.101.2362, per-user non-elevated GitHub installation, Windows build 26200, with a diagnostic ZIP attached.
Original reporter observed the issue roughly every two or three days.
Latest comment on 2026-09-24 reports Awake and Command Palette enabling unexpectedly while only FancyZones and PowerRename were intended to be enabled.
The issue has no linked fix PR or confirmed owning symbol.
inferences: A shared settings persistence, migration, or startup-state path may be involved, but this is not confirmed.
The cross-module report makes a LightSwitch-only design premature.
issue_context.analysis: Revalidation preserves the useful original diagnostic evidence while recognizing that the newest report broadens the symptom. The next decision is whether the state change follows startup/update/recovery or a settings-file write; a narrowly targeted recurrence report can distinguish those paths.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body and all seven current comments, including the 2026-09-24 cross-module report.
Confirmed no linked PR, assignee, or concrete code path is present in the public record.
Preserved the existing diagnostic finding that no matching crash/error signature was detected.

actions.label: Request state-change trigger and fresh diagnostics

comment.body:
Thanks for the original diagnostic ZIP and for clarifying that the LightSwitch reset recurs every few days. The newer report that Awake and Command Palette can also become enabled broadens the symptom, but the public discussion still does not show which lifecycle event or settings write precedes the change. Please provide:
1. Whether the change follows a restart, PowerToys update, crash recovery, sleep/resume, or another specific event, and list the exact modules whose state changed.
2. After the next occurrence, add a comment containing /bugreport immediately so the current settings and startup diagnostics are captured.
This will distinguish a startup/migration path from an ongoing settings-persistence problem before maintainers choose a code fix.
